name: Haiku concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Software and platform-led AI infrastructure thesis with selective semiconductor exposure, balancing proven enterprise platforms (MSFT, CRM, PLTR) against chip concentration risk.
reassessment_note: Current book entered Sept 8 with 82% concentration in pure semiconductors (NVDA 27%, ASML 15%, AMD 15%, QCOM 9%, SOXL 10%), timing proved poor as AI sentiment inverted Sept 12 on Amodei's slowdown message. Portfolio now underwater -2.12% with positions suffering 5-15% drawdowns. Macro headwind tomorrow (FOMC likely +0.25bp) creates additional risk for capital-intensive chip exposure. Rotating to software/platforms thesis (MSFT +18%, CRM +10%, PLTR +10%) reduces correlation to chip sector weakness while maintaining AI infrastructure conviction. Trimming NVDA to 15%, ASML to 8%, AMD to 8%, eliminating SOXL leverage. ASML's raised 2026 guidance (€43-45B) supports smaller core holding. Increasing cash to 26% for flexibility post-FOMC. Differentiates from Round 2's platform bias through heavier MSFT/PLTR weighting and complete elimination of SOXL.

positions.thesis: Cloud infrastructure and AI platform services (Copilot, Azure AI) less vulnerable to chip sentiment shifts. Held firm during recent AI sell-off, outperforming semiconductors. Enterprise stickiness and recurring revenue model provide stability ahead of rate decision.

Trimmed from 27% to limit concentration risk in capital-intensive chip buildout. Core position maintained on AI training infrastructure demand and data center TAM expansion, but ASML guidance and customer guidance suggest pace sustainable rather than accelerating.

Enterprise AI software plays are resilient to macro pressure. CRM's AI Cloud and Einstein platform integrate AI into customer operations independent of chip capex cycles. Software-as-a-service model has lower duration risk than semiconductor.

AI tools and data platform for enterprises. Differentiation play - benefits from enterprise AI adoption without direct chip concentration. Software-driven moat and recurring revenue. Held despite narrow loss, positioned for wider AI deployment across organizations.

Reduced from 15% to 8% given -9.79% loss and timing risk, but raised 2026 guidance (€43-45B) reinforces AI chip demand durability. Core holding at smaller scale respects both fundamental support and technical weakness.

Trimmed from 15% to 8% to reduce chip sector concentration. Secondary play to NVDA. Strong Q2 earnings beat supports position but reduced weight reflects execution risk and broader semiconductor sentiment.

Minimal holding. While Zacks consensus expects FY2026 revenue down 2.8%, mobile and edge AI deployment remain drivers. Kept as small diversifier but not conviction sized given negative guidance revisions.
